page: Microsoft Azure E96as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system features a dedicated CPU allocation with hyper-threading enabled, supported by 768.0 GB of RAM, which yields a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no integrated GPU or local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data places the E96as_v7 in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Geekbench metrics. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with small-block read-only and large-block write operations scoring in the top tier. Database operations and memory-bound tasks perform exceptionally well, with Redis SET operations reaching 139.15 million operations per second. However, while small and medium LLM inference speeds rank in the top tier, prompt processing for large 70B models drops to average tier performance, representing a notable tradeoff for large-scale AI workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of memory relative to vCPUs provides a balanced resource profile for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. This makes the server suitable for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching, software compilation, and medium-scale language model inference. The lack of local storage requires external storage attachments, which should be factored into the overall infrastructure design.
